chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father - from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

«Do not let your glance pass beyond the place of your prostration during the prayer.» And he said, «A man should not pray with his buttons undone if he is not wearing an izar (lower garment).» Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating recommendation (istihbab), and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.طَرَفُ الْعَيْنِ: the corner of the eye / glance

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes regarding gaze and clothing during Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted through the chain of Ghayath ibn Ibrahim, establishes two specific etiquettes (adab) for prayer: maintaining gaze within the prostration area and ensuring the lower garment is buttoned if not fully covered. Shaykh al-Tusi includes the commentary of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Furat al-Qummi, who clarifies that these rulings are recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both outward decorum and inner concentration during worship.
